Tosafot on Bava Batra 115b:2:1.english: Even the Nasi of Israel - who wishes to institute an arrangement according to the need of the hour, similar to what we found regarding the Benjaminites, who stipulated that a son's daughter should not inherit together with his brother [i.e., her father's brother, her uncle] — we do not listen to him, because of the Sadducees:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 115b:4:1.hebrew: מלמד שבא צבעון על אמו והוליד ממנה ענה - קשה לר"ת: דאמאי אהדר ליה מענה? דלמא בן הבן הוי כבנו, אבל בת בנו לא תהיה כבנו אלא כבתו. ונראה לר"ת דענה אשה היתה, כדמוכחי קראי, דכתיב: "ואלה בני אהליבמה בת ענה בת צבעון" — אלמא אשה היתה. וליכא למימר דענה אחר היה, דהא אמר הכא דצבעון הוליד ענה. ועוד, דמיד אחר קרא דמייתי הכא "הוא ענה אשר מצא וגו'" כתיב: "אלה בני ענה דישן ואהליבמה בת ענה". והשתא אהדר להו שפיר ר' יוחנן בן זכאי, דבת הבן חשובה כבן לירש עם שאר בנים, שהן קודמין לבת — מדקרי ליה "יושבי הארץ". וכך היא קודמת לבת, ומכאן סותר לבסוף ק"ו שלהן. והא דכתיב "הוא ענה" בלשון זכר, היינו משום שירשה עם אחי צבעון כזכר. וא"ת: והיאך ירשה ענה, והלא היה לה אח, וכתיב: "ובני צבעון איה וענה"? וי"ל: דמת איה; תדע, מדלא חשיב בני איה כדחשיב בני ענה. ורש"י פירש בפירוש חומש דאהליבמה היתה בת ענה ובת צבעון, וכי היכי דאמר הכא שבא צבעון על אמו והוליד ממנה ענה, ולכך חשיב ליה בני שעיר, הכי נמי בא ענה על אמו והוליד ממנה אהליבמה, ולהכי קרי לה אהליבמה בת ענה בת צבעון:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 115b:4:1.english: This teaches that Tzibeon had relations with his mother and fathered Anah from her - Rabbeinu Tam found this difficult: Why did [Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai] answer them from [the verse about] Anah? Perhaps a son's son is considered like one's son, but a son's daughter would not be considered like one's son, but rather like one's daughter. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that Anah was a woman, as the verses prove, for it is written: "And these are the sons of Oholivamah, daughter of Anah, daughter of Tzibeon" (Genesis 36:14) — evidently she was a woman. And one cannot say that this was a different Anah, for [the Gemara] says here that Tzibeon fathered Anah. Furthermore, immediately after the verse that is cited here, "This is the Anah who found [the hot springs] etc.," it is written: "These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholivamah, daughter of Anah" (Genesis 36:25). And now Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai answered them well: that a son's daughter is considered like a son, to inherit together with the other sons, who take precedence over a daughter — since [the verse] calls him [Anah] one of "the inhabitants of the land." And so she takes precedence over a daughter, and from here he ultimately refutes their kal vachomer. And as for the fact that it is written "This is Anah" in the masculine, that is because she inherited like a male together with the brothers of Tzibeon [i.e., her uncles]. And if you ask: How could Anah inherit, when she had a brother, and it is written: "And the sons of Tzibeon: Ayah and Anah" (Genesis 36:24)? One can answer: that Ayah had died. Know this [to be so] from the fact that [the verse] does not enumerate the sons of Ayah as it enumerates the sons of Anah. And Rashi explained in his commentary on Chumash that Oholivamah was the daughter of Anah and also the daughter of Tzibeon; just as [the Gemara] says here that Tzibeon had relations with his mother and fathered Anah from her, and therefore [the verse] counts him among the sons of Seir, so too Anah had relations with his mother and fathered Oholivamah from her, and therefore [the verse] calls her "Oholivamah, daughter of Anah, daughter of Tzibeon."
